taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: deciduous shrub, 1-2.5 m. high.

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Philadelphus lewisii: an erect to spreading shrub that grows 3 to 10 feet (1-3 m) tall.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: a shrub.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: a shrub, the bark of the previous season with cross cracks, eventually exfoliating.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: deciduous shrub.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Leaves in opposite pairs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 145556822, 167614209, 128686264, 227021248, 165384019, 25848239, 166346362, 7747): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: leaves ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2-5 cm. long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 1.2 cm to 3 cm wide, about half as wide as long as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 2 mm to 6 mm long.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: leaves ovate or ovate-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: acute at apex.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 384, Philadelphus lewisii: entire or denticulate; read as entire, as most of the photos show.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 385, Philadelphus lewisii: flower clusters racemose.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: FEIS species review, Philadelphus lewisii: the showy flowers occur in clusters of three to fifteen.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: racemes 3 cm to 8 cm long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 385, Philadelphus lewisii: petals elliptic to oval, 10-15 mm. long, so the open flower about 2.5 cm to 3.5 cm across.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 385, Philadelphus lewisii: petals elliptic to oval, 10-15 mm. long.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Four petals to a flower, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 145556822, 167614209, 128686264, 227021248, 165384019, 25848239, 166346362, 7747): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_colour.note: Petals white; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 145556822, 167614209, 128686264, 227021248, 165384019, 25848239, 166346362, 7747): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Philadelphus lewisii: the fruit is a four-chambered capsule.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS species review, Philadelphus lewisii: capsule about 0.24 to 0.39 inch (0.6-1 cm) long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 385, Philadelphus lewisii: flowering May to July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe in August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a many-stemmed rounded shrub of ascending branches, bright green opposite leaves, white four-petalled flowers in short clusters at the twig tips.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Lewis's mock orange from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 2.0 m tall at 12 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, phase C batch 3 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from Abrams, FEIS and Dendrology, counts from photos.
